# Obsolete and deprecated elements

## Obsolete and deprecated elements

### `<acronym>`

Allows authors to clearly indicate a sequence of characters that compose an acronym or abbreviation for a word. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/acronym>

### `<big>`

Renders the enclosed text at a font size one level larger than the surrounding text (`medium` becomes `large`, for example). The size is capped at the browser's maximum permitted font size. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/big>

### `<center>`

Displays its block-level or inline contents centered horizontally within its containing element. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/center>

### `<dir>`

Container for a directory of files and/or folders, potentially with styles and icons applied by the user agent. Do not use this obsolete element; instead, you should use the `<ul>` element for lists, including lists of files. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dir>

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `compact` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This Boolean attribute hints that the list should be rendered in a compact style.

### `<fencedframe>`

Represents a nested browsing context, like `<iframe>` but with more native privacy features built in. _(deprecated, Limited availability)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/fencedframe>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| Content categories | Flow content, phrasing content, embedded content, interactive content, palpable content. |
| Permitted content | None. |
| Tag omission | None, both the starting and ending tag are mandatory. |
| Permitted parents | Any element that accepts embedded content. |
| Implicit ARIA role | No corresponding role |
| Permitted ARIA roles | `application`, `document`, `img`, `none`, `presentation` |
| DOM interface | `HTMLFencedFrameElement` |

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `allow` — Specifies a Permissions Policy for the `<fencedframe>`, which defines what features are available to the `<fencedframe>` based on the origin of the request.
- `height` — A unitless integer representing the height of the fenced frame in CSS pixels.
- `width` — A unitless integer representing the width of the fenced frame in CSS pixels.

### `<font>`

Defines the font size, color and face for its content. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/font>

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `color` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute sets the text color using either a named color or a color specified in the hexadecimal #RRGGBB format.
- `face` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute contains a comma-separated list of one or more font names.
- `size` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute specifies the font size as either a numeric or relative value.

### `<frame>`

Defines a particular area in which another HTML document can be displayed. A frame should be used within a `<frameset>`. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/frame>

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `src` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute specifies the document that will be displayed by the frame.
- `name` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute is used for labeling frames.
- `noresize` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute prevents resizing of frames by users.
- `scrolling` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute defines the existence of a scrollbar.
- `marginheight` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute defines the height of the margin between frames.
- `marginwidth` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute defines the width of the margin between frames.
- `frameborder` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute allows you to specify a frame's border.

### `<frameset>`

Used to contain `<frame>` elements. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/frameset>

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `cols` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute specifies the number and size of horizontal spaces in a frameset.
- `rows` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — This attribute specifies the number and size of vertical spaces in a frameset.

### `<marquee>`

Used to insert a scrolling area of text. You can control what happens when the text reaches the edges of its content area using its attributes. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/marquee>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| DOM interface | `HTMLMarqueeElement` |

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `behavior` _(deprecated)_ — Sets how the text is scrolled within the marquee.
- `bgcolor` _(deprecated)_ — Sets the background color through color name or hexadecimal value.
- `direction` _(deprecated)_ — Sets the direction of the scrolling within the marquee.
- `height` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the height in pixels or percentage value.
- `hspace` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the horizontal margin
- `loop` _(deprecated)_ — Sets the number of times the marquee will scroll.
- `scrollamount` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the amount of scrolling at each interval in pixels.
- `scrolldelay` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the interval between each scroll movement in milliseconds.
- `truespeed` _(deprecated)_ — By default, `scrolldelay` values lower than 60 are ignored.
- `vspace` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the vertical margin in pixels or percentage value.
- `width` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Sets the width in pixels or percentage value.

### `<nobr>`

Prevents the text it contains from automatically wrapping across multiple lines, potentially resulting in the user having to scroll horizontally to see the entire width of the text. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/nobr>

### `<noembed>`

An obsolete, non-standard way to provide alternative, or "fallback", content for browsers that do not support the embed element or do not support the type of embedded content an author wishes to use. This element was deprecated in HTML 4.01 and above in favor of placing fallback content between the opening and closing tags of an `<object>` element. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/noembed>

### `<noframes>`

Provides content to be presented in browsers that don't support (or have disabled support for) the `<frame>` element. Although most commonly-used browsers support frames, there are exceptions, including certain special-use browsers including some mobile browsers, as well as text-mode browsers. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/noframes>

### `<param>`

Defines parameters for an `<object>` element. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/param>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| Content categories | None. |
| Permitted content | None; it is a void element. |
| Tag omission | Must have a start tag and must not have an end tag. |
| Permitted parents | An `<object>` before any flow content. |
| Implicit ARIA role | No corresponding role |
| Permitted ARIA roles | No `role` permitted |
| DOM interface | `HTMLParamElement` |

**Attributes** (plus global attributes):

- `name` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Name of the parameter.
- `value` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Specifies the value of the parameter.
- `type` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Only used if the `valuetype` is set to `ref`.
- `valuetype` _(deprecated, non-standard)_ — Specifies the type of the `value` attribute.

### `<plaintext>`

Renders everything following the start tag as raw text, ignoring any following HTML. There is no closing tag, since everything after it is considered raw text. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/plaintext>

### `<rb>`

Used to delimit the base text component of a ruby annotation, i.e., the text that is being annotated. One `<rb>` element should wrap each separate atomic segment of the base text. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/rb>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| Content categories | None. |
| Permitted content | As a child of a `<ruby>` element. |
| Tag omission | The end tag can be omitted if the element is immediately followed by an `<rt>`, `<rtc>`, or `<rp>` element or another `<rb>` element, or if there is no more content in the parent element. |
| Permitted parents | A `<ruby>` element. |
| Permitted ARIA roles | Any |
| DOM interface | `HTMLElement` |

### `<rtc>`

Embraces semantic annotations of characters presented in a ruby of `<rb>` elements used inside of `<ruby>` element. `<rb>` elements can have both pronunciation (`<rt>`) and semantic (`<rtc>`) annotations. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/rtc>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| Content categories | None. |
| Permitted content | Phrasing content or `<rt>` elements. |
| Tag omission | The closing tag can be omitted if it is immediately followed by a `<rb>`, `<rtc>` or `<rt>` element opening tag or by its parent closing tag. |
| Permitted parents | A `<ruby>` element. |
| Permitted ARIA roles | Any |
| DOM interface | `HTMLElement` |

### `<strike>`

Places a strikethrough (horizontal line) over text. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/strike>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| DOM interface | `HTMLElement` |

### `<tt>`

Creates inline text which is presented using the user agent default monospace font face. This element was created for the purpose of rendering text as it would be displayed on a fixed-width display such as a teletype, text-only screen, or line printer. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/tt>

| Technical summary |  |
| --- | --- |
| Content categories | Flow content, phrasing content, palpable content. |
| Permitted content | Phrasing content. |
| Tag omission | None, both the starting and ending tag are mandatory. |
| Permitted parents | Any element that accepts phrasing content. |
| Permitted ARIA roles | Any |
| DOM interface | `HTMLElement` |

### `<xmp>`

Renders text between the start and end tags without interpreting the HTML in between and using a monospaced font. The HTML2 specification recommended that it should be rendered wide enough to allow 80 characters per line. _(deprecated)_

MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/xmp>
